dialogueClips.text: Do you like the park, Ana?
dialogueClips.speaker: kim

dialogueClips.text: Yes, I do! I love the park. And you?
dialogueClips.speaker: ana

dialogueClips.text: Me too. I like music and books.
dialogueClips.speaker: kim

dialogueClips.text: Books? I don’t like books. I like soccer!
dialogueClips.speaker: ana

dialogueClips.text: Soccer? Cool!
dialogueClips.speaker: kim

dialogueClips.text: Hi, Ana! Where are you?
dialogueClips.speaker: kim

dialogueClips.text: Hi, Kim! I’m in Porto. I’m working here this week.
dialogueClips.speaker: ana

dialogueClips.text: Do you usually work in Porto?
dialogueClips.speaker: kim

dialogueClips.text: No, I don’t. I usually work from home.
dialogueClips.speaker: ana

dialogueClips.text: What are you doing now?
dialogueClips.speaker: kim

dialogueClips.text: I’m drinking coffee next to the river. I have a meeting at ten.
dialogueClips.speaker: ana

dialogueClips.text: Nice! I’m walking in the…
dialogueClips.speaker: kim

dialogueClips.text: Sorry? Can you say that again? Kim? Kim?
dialogueClips.speaker: ana

dialogueClips.text: Ana, what was your best trip?
dialogueClips.speaker: kim

dialogueClips.text: A weekend in Ilhabela with my brother, Leo. The best part was the boat trip.
dialogueClips.speaker: ana

dialogueClips.text: Nice! Did anything go wrong?
dialogueClips.speaker: kim

dialogueClips.text: Yes! It rained all day on Sunday, so we played cards at the hotel. What about you?
dialogueClips.speaker: ana

dialogueClips.text: My best day out was a Sunday in Bom Retiro, in São Paulo. It felt like home!
dialogueClips.speaker: kim

dialogueClips.text: I love that! Where would you like to go next?
dialogueClips.speaker: ana

dialogueClips.text: I’d love to go to Salvador. The food looks amazing!
dialogueClips.speaker: kim

dialogueClips.text: So, how’s the new job going? Do you go to the office every day?
dialogueClips.speaker: kim

dialogueClips.text: Three days a week. What I like about the office is the people. I learn so much from my team.
dialogueClips.speaker: ana

dialogueClips.text: I see your point, but I’d rather stay home. No commute, no noise, and I take a break when I want.
dialogueClips.speaker: kim

dialogueClips.text: Don’t you feel lonely sometimes?
dialogueClips.speaker: ana

dialogueClips.text: It depends on the week. On a good day, I finish early and go for a walk.
dialogueClips.speaker: kim

dialogueClips.text: For me, a good day is when I get things done and still have time for my friends.
dialogueClips.speaker: ana

dialogueClips.text: Exactly. Work is important, but it’s not everything.
dialogueClips.speaker: kim

dialogueClips.text: So, how was New York?
dialogueClips.speaker: kim

dialogueClips.text: Pretty good, but on the second day, my phone died at four in the afternoon.
dialogueClips.speaker: ana

dialogueClips.text: Oh no! Why?
dialogueClips.speaker: kim

dialogueClips.text: I’d been using it as a map all day, and I didn’t notice how low the battery was. And I’d left my charger at the hotel.
dialogueClips.speaker: ana

dialogueClips.text: Why didn’t you go back to the hotel?
dialogueClips.speaker: kim

dialogueClips.text: I tried, but I got lost. And the team dinner was at seven. The address was in a message from Raj!
dialogueClips.speaker: ana

dialogueClips.text: So what did you do?
dialogueClips.speaker: kim

dialogueClips.text: I asked a doorman for help, and he told me about a café. But there were no free outlets.
dialogueClips.speaker: ana

dialogueClips.text: Oh no. And then?
dialogueClips.speaker: kim

dialogueClips.text: I’d been waiting there alone for twenty minutes when a woman lent me her power bank. Luckily, I had my cable.
dialogueClips.speaker: ana

dialogueClips.text: So did you make it to the dinner?
dialogueClips.speaker: kim

dialogueClips.text: Eventually, yes. I caught a taxi and got there at eight. By then, they’d been waiting for an hour!
dialogueClips.speaker: ana
